targets.title: Motion as Motivation: Using Repetitive Flexion Movements to Stimulate the Approach System.
targets.evidence_quote: Study 1 was a direct replication that used the same task, equipment, and experimental computer design as Haeffel ( 2011 ).
targets.outcome_quote: We conducted two studies to test the effect of repeated flexion finger movements on approach motivation. The results of the two studies were inconsistent with each other as well as with the original Haeffel ( 2011 ) study (see Figure 1 ).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors judge the two studies inconsistent with the original and argue significant effects are likely chance. Neither replication recovers the original BAS-Fun and gender-dependent persistence findings; significant findings occur on different outcomes. Maxwell and Davidson supplied the adapted task rather than the finding directly retested.
